1.word_for_word: चतुर्दशे अद्भुतं दृष्ट्वा — in the fourteenth chapter, having seen the wonder; पूर्वागन्तुक-निश्चयम् — and determined what had previously occurred; अनीशः कर्तुम् — unable to do anything; ब्रह्मा विमोहितः — bewildered Brahmā; अस्तौषीत् कृष्णम् — praised Kṛṣṇa; स्व-कृतापराधेन भिया स-कम्पतया — trembling from fear because of his own offense; भगवन्-महिमानम् अनवगाहमानः — unable to fathom Bhagavān’s majesty; दृष्ट-स्वरूपम् एव कीर्तयन् — praising the form he had just seen; नौमि — I bow/praise; हे ईड्य — O praiseworthy One; ते तुभ्यं नौमि — I bow to You; अभ्रवत् वपुः — whose body is like a raincloud; तडिद्-वद् अम्बरम् — whose garment is like lightning; गुञ्जा-अवतंस-बर्हापीडैः लसन् मुखम् — whose face shines with guñjā earrings and peacock-feather crest; वन्याः स्रजः — whose garlands are of forest flowers; कवलादिभिः लक्ष्मभिः श्रीः — whose beauty is marked by the morsel of food and the other cowherd signs; मृदू पादौ — whose feet are tender; पशुपस्य अङ्गजाय — to the son of the cowherd.
1.translation: In the fourteenth chapter Brahmā, having witnessed the astonishing manifestation and understood what had occurred, found himself powerless and, still bewildered, praised Kṛṣṇa. Trembling with fear because of his offense and unable to fathom the Lord’s greatness, he began simply by describing the form before him: ‘O worshipful One, I bow to You.’ Kṛṣṇa’s body was dark like a raincloud, His garment flashed like lightning, His face shone beneath guñjā ornaments and a peacock-feather crest, He wore a garland of forest flowers, and His beauty bore the distinctive signs of the cowherd boy—the morsel of food and the rest. His feet were tender; He was the son of the cowherd Nanda.

2.word_for_word: अस्यापि तव वपुषः — even of this body of Yours; सुलभत्वेन प्रकाशितस्य अपि — though manifested as easily accessible; महि महिमानम् अवसितुं — to comprehend its greatness; अहम् अपि न ईशे — even I am unable; मद्-अनुग्रहम् — produced by Your favor toward me; स्वेच्छा-मयस्य — existing by Your own will; भक्तानां यथा यथा इच्छा तथा तथा भवतः — becoming in whatever manner Your devotees desire; न तु भूत-मयस्य — not made of material elements; अचिन्त्य-शुद्ध-सत्त्वात्मकस्य — constituted of inconceivable pure sattva; केवलस्य आत्म-सुखानुभूतेः — of You whose nature is the experience of Your own bliss; गुणातीतस्य — beyond the guṇas; आन्तरेण निरुद्धेन मनसा अपि — even by a mind withdrawn within; को ज्ञातुं समर्थः — who could know Your greatness?; अथवा भूत-मयस्य विराड्-रूपस्य अपि — alternatively, even the greatness of the elemental cosmic form; कोऽपि नेशे — no one can fully measure; किं पुनः तव असाधारणस्य — how much less Your unique form beyond controller-controlled duality.
2.translation: Brahmā explains why his praise can only begin from what he sees. Even this body of Kṛṣṇa, though mercifully manifested in an accessible form, cannot have its greatness fully comprehended by Brahmā. It is manifested by the Lord’s favor and by His own free will, taking whatever form His devotees desire; it is not composed of material elements but of inconceivable pure sattva. If even a mind withdrawn from the senses cannot measure the greatness of the transcendent Lord whose nature is His own bliss, who could do so? Alternatively, if no one can fully know even the vast elemental cosmic form ruled by Him, what need be said of His own unique form, beyond the distinction of ruler and ruled?

3.word_for_word: अज्ञाः कथं संसारं तरेयुः — how then can the ignorant cross saṃsāra?; ज्ञानम् उदपास्य — putting aside speculative knowledge, not laboring at it even slightly; सद्भिः मुखरितां भवदीय-वार्ताम् — the narration concerning You sounded forth by the saints; स्व-स्व-स्थान एव स्थिताः — remaining in their own proper station; स्वत एव श्रुति-गताम् — which comes naturally to their hearing; तनु-वाङ्-मनोभिः नमन्तः सत्-कुर्वन्तः — honoring it with body, speech and mind; केवलं जीवन्ति — simply living in that way; त्रि-लोक्याम् अजितः अपि त्वं जितः — though unconquerable, You are conquered by them in the three worlds.
3.translation: How, then, can those without such knowledge cross saṃsāra? By abandoning the exhausting attempt to grasp You through speculation and simply remaining in their own station while hearing the accounts of You spoken by saints. When those accounts naturally reach their ears, they honor them with body, speech and mind and live by them. By such persons, though You are otherwise unconquerable, You become conquered. What need is there for the labor of speculative knowledge?

4.word_for_word: भक्तिं विना ज्ञानं नैव सिध्येत् — without devotion knowledge does not succeed; श्रेयः-स्रुतिम् — devotion from which streams all auspicious attainment and liberation, or the path of all welfare; तां ते भक्तिम् उदस्य — abandoning that devotion to You; तेषां क्लेशलः क्लेश एव अवशिष्यते — for them only suffering remains; अल्पं धान्यं परित्यज्य तुषान् अवघ्नन्ति — like discarding the little grain and beating husks empty of kernels; न किञ्चित् फलम् — there is no fruit; भक्तिं तुच्छीकृत्य केवल-बोधाय प्रयतन्ते — so too those who belittle devotion and strive only for abstract knowledge.
4.translation: Knowledge does not reach perfection without devotion. Bhakti is the stream from which the goods of this world and liberation flow, or the very road of all true welfare. Those who abandon devotion to You and labor for knowledge alone are left only with the labor itself. They are like people who throw away the grain and then beat empty husks: no fruit results. So it is with those who belittle bhakti and strive for bare cognition.

5.word_for_word: भक्त्यैव ज्ञानम् — knowledge comes through devotion alone; सद्-आचारं प्रमाणयति — he cites the conduct of the saints as evidence; योगिनः अपि योगैः ज्ञानम् अप्राप्य — yogins who had failed to attain knowledge through yogic means; त्वद्-अर्पितेहाः — whose activities, even worldly ones, were offered to You; निज-कर्म-लब्धया — through what was gained by their own duties offered to You; कथोपनीतया भक्त्या — by devotion brought near through hearing Your narrations; विबुध्य विश्व-व्यापकं आत्मानम् — realizing the Self that pervades the universe; अञ्जः परां गतिं प्राप्ताः — easily attained Your supreme destination.
5.translation: The experience of earlier saints confirms that knowledge arises through devotion, not otherwise. Yogins who had not attained true knowledge by yoga later offered even their ordinary activities to You. Through duties offered to You and through bhakti brought near by hearing Your narrations, they realized the Self pervading the universe and easily attained Your supreme destination.

6.word_for_word: स-गुण-निर्गुणयोर् उभयोर् अपि ज्ञानं दुर्घटम् — both the qualified and unqualified aspects are difficult to know; त्वत्-कथा-श्रवणादिना एव त्वत्-प्राप्तिः — You are attained through hearing Your stories and the like; गुणातीतस्य ज्ञानं कथञ्चित् भवेत् — the aspect beyond attributes may in some way be conceptually known; न तु सगुणस्य तव — but not the personal Lord endowed with qualities; अचिन्त्यानन्त-गुणत्वात् — because Your qualities are inconceivable and infinite; अमलैर् अन्तरात्मभिः प्रत्याहृत-इन्द्रियैः — by purified inner faculties with senses withdrawn; महिमा विबोद्धुं अर्हति — Your greatness may become an object of realization; स्वानुभवात् — by direct inward realization; अविक्रियात् — free of particular modifications; अरूपतः — not an external object; अनन्य-बोध्यात्मतया स्व-प्रकाशत्वेन — self-revealing because known by no awareness other than itself; लक्ष्मीः अपि — even Lakṣmī; अगुणस्य ते महिमानम् वस्तुतः विबोद्धुं न अर्हति — cannot delimit the true greatness of You beyond the guṇas.
6.translation: It has been said that both the Lord with attributes and the reality beyond attributes are difficult to know, and that He is attained through hearing His narrations and similar bhakti. Brahmā now adds that the transcendence of qualities may perhaps be apprehended in some fashion, but the Lord endowed with inconceivably infinite qualities cannot be measured. His greatness may be realized inwardly by purified, withdrawn faculties through direct experience, not as an external object but as self-luminous awareness free from limiting forms. On another reading, even Lakṣmī, though perfectly pure within, cannot comprehend His limitless glory as it truly is; it is known only by the Lord’s own self-revelation.

7.word_for_word: गुणात्मनः — of You, the ground and ruler of all qualities; गुणान् विमातुम् — to measure or count the qualities; के ईशिरे — who has ever been capable?; विश्वस्य हिताय बहु-गुणाविष्कारेण अवतीर्णस्य — of You who descend displaying many qualities for the world’s welfare; भू-परमाणवः विमिताः भवेयुः — perhaps experts could count the atoms of the earth; खे मिहिका हिम-कणाः — the particles of mist or snow in the sky; द्यु-भासः नक्षत्रादि-किरण-परमाणवः — even the particles of stellar rays in heaven; तव गुणाः न — but not Your qualities.
7.translation: Who has ever been able even to count the qualities of You who are their very ground and ruler, and who descend displaying innumerable qualities for the welfare of the universe? Given vast time and consummate skill, one might perhaps count the atoms of the earth, the particles of mist or snow in the sky, or even the particles of the rays of the stars; Your qualities cannot be numbered.

8.word_for_word: भक्तिर् एव सङ्गच्छते — devotion alone is appropriate; ते अनुकम्पां सुसमीक्षमाणः — one who earnestly looks for Your compassion; ‘तव कृपा कदा भविष्यति’ इति बहु-मन्यमानः — regarding Your coming mercy as everything; स्वार्जितं कर्म-फलम् अनासक्तः भुञ्जानः — accepting without attachment the fruit of his own past actions; न अतीव-तप-आदिना क्लिश्यन् — not tormenting himself with extreme austerity; एवं जीवेत — living in this way; मुक्तौ दाय-भाग् भवति — becomes an heir entitled to liberation; भक्तस्य जीवन-व्यतिरेकेण न अन्यद् उपयुज्यते — for a devotee nothing beyond such a surrendered life is required, as an heir needs no extra act to receive an inheritance.
8.translation: Therefore bhakti alone is fitting. One who keeps looking for Your compassion, thinking, ‘When will Your mercy come?’ and who accepts without attachment the results of his own past actions, without tormenting himself by extreme austerities, becomes an heir to liberation. Just as inheritance comes to the rightful heir by relationship, nothing beyond the devotee’s surrendered way of life is needed to make him eligible for liberation.

9.word_for_word: स्वापराधं निवेदयति — Brahmā confesses his offense; मे अनार्यं दौर्जन्यं पश्य — see my ignoble wickedness; मायिनाम् अपि मायिनि विमोहके त्वयि — toward You, the deluder even of masters of māyā; स्व-मायां प्रसार्य — extending my own māyā; आत्म-वैभवम् ईक्षितुम् ऐच्छम् — I wished to test/display my own power; त्वयि अहं कियान् — what am I before You?; न किञ्चित् — nothing at all; अग्नेर् उद्भूता ज्वाला अग्नौ न किञ्चित् — as a flame born from fire is nothing separate before the fire itself.
9.translation: Having praised the Lord, Brahmā confesses his offense: ‘O Lord, behold my ignoble conduct. Against You, who bewilder even the masters of māyā, I spread my own little māyā because I wished to see the extent of my own power. What am I before You? Nothing at all—just as a flame that has arisen from fire is nothing independent when set against the fire itself.’

10.word_for_word: रजो-भुवः — born from rajas; अजानतः — ignorant; अज-अवलेप-अन्ध-तमः-अन्ध-चक्षुषः — whose vision was blinded by the dense darkness of pride, thinking ‘I am the unborn creator of the world’; त्वत्तः पृथग्-ईश-मानिनः — imagining myself a lord separate from You; अन्यत्र प्रभुत्वेन वर्तमानः अपि — though exercising lordship elsewhere; मयि नाथे सति नाथवान् मद्-भृत्यः एव अयम् — before You, my Lord, I am merely a dependent servant; अतः अनुकम्प्यः — therefore worthy of compassion; क्षमस्व — forgive me.
10.translation: Brahmā calls himself one born from rajas, ignorant and blinded by the dense darkness of pride—the conceit, ‘I am the unborn creator of the universe.’ He had imagined himself an independent lord apart from Kṛṣṇa. Yet however much authority he exercises elsewhere, before the true Lord he is only a dependent servant. ‘Therefore regard me as an object of compassion and forgive me.’

11.word_for_word: तमः प्रकृतिः, महान्, अहङ्कारः, खं, चरः वायुः, अग्निः, वार् जलम्, भूः — prakṛti, mahat, ahaṅkāra, ether, air, fire, water and earth; एतैः संवेष्टितः अण्ड-घटः — the cosmic egg enclosed by these layers; तस्मिन् स्व-मानेन सप्त-वितस्तिः कायः यस्य सोऽहम् — I whose body measures only seven spans within that egg; क्व अहम् क्व ते महित्वम् — what am I and what is Your greatness?; अविगणितानि अण्डानि — innumerable universes; तव रोम-विवराणि — Your hair-pores are like openings; तेषां चर्याय वाताध्वानः — winds pass through them as those universes move.
11.translation: Brahmā contrasts his scale with the Lord’s. The cosmic egg is wrapped in prakṛti, mahat, ahaṅkāra, ether, air, fire, water and earth, and within it Brahmā’s own body is only seven spans by his measure. What is he compared with Kṛṣṇa’s greatness? Innumerable cosmic eggs move like particles through the channels of His hair-pores. Brahmā is therefore exceedingly insignificant and fit only for the Lord’s compassion.

12.word_for_word: गर्भ-गतस्य शिशोः पादयोर् उत्क्षेपणम् — the kicking of a child within the womb; मातुः किम् अपराधाय — is it an offense against the mother?; अस्ति-नास्ति... स्थूल-सूक्ष्म-कार्य-कारण-शब्दैः अभिहितम् — everything denoted by words of existence/nonexistence, gross/subtle, effect/cause; सर्वं वस्तु — all reality so described; तव कुक्षेः अन्तर् बहिः किञ्चित् अस्ति? — is anything at all inside or outside Your womb/body separately from You?; न किञ्चित् — nothing; सर्वस्य तव कुक्षि-गतत्वेन मम अपि — since everything, including me, is contained in You; मातृ-वद् अपराधः सोढव्यः — my offense should be borne as a mother bears the movements of a child in her womb.
12.translation: Brahmā asks whether a child kicking inside its mother’s womb is regarded as offending her. Everything described by the language of existence and nonexistence, gross and subtle, effect and cause is contained in the Lord; nothing lies separately inside or outside Him. Since Brahmā too exists within Him, the Lord should bear Brahmā’s offense as a mother bears the movements of the child in her womb.

13.word_for_word: विशेषतः अपि त्वत्तः मम जन्म प्रसिद्धम् — in particular, my birth from You is well known; जगत्-त्रयस्य अन्ते प्रलये उदधीनां संप्लवे — at the dissolution of the three worlds when the oceans merge; नारायणस्य उदरे — in Nārāyaṇa’s belly/waters; तस्य नालात् अजः विनिर्गतः — the unborn Brahmā emerged from His lotus-stalk; या वाक् सा मृषा न भवति — that scriptural statement is certainly not false; त्वत्तः अहं किं न विनिर्गतः? — did I not then arise from You?; त्वत्तः एव उत्पन्नः — I was indeed born from You.
13.translation: Brahmā’s dependence is especially evident from the well-known account of his own birth. At cosmic dissolution, amid the merged oceans, the unborn Brahmā emerged from the lotus-stalk arising from Nārāyaṇa. That scriptural statement cannot be false. Thus Brahmā asks rhetorically: ‘Did I not in fact arise from You? I certainly did.’

14.word_for_word: नारायणस् त्वम् — You Yourself are Nārāyaṇa; सर्व-देहिनाम् आत्मा असि — You are the Self of all embodied beings; नारं जीव-समूहः, अयनम् आश्रयः यस्य — Nārāyaṇa is He whose abode/support is the aggregate of beings; अधीशः प्रवर्तकः — the supreme controller who sets them in motion; नारस्य अयनं प्रवृत्तिः यस्मात् — He from whom the movement/course of beings proceeds; अखिल-लोक-साक्षी — witness of all worlds; नारम् अयसे जानासि — You ‘go to/know’ all beings; प्रसिद्धो नारायणः अपि तव अङ्गं मूर्तिः — even the conventionally named Nārāyaṇa is a form/limb of You; नराद् उद्भूतानि तत्त्वानि नाराणि — principles arisen from Nara are called nāras; तेषाम् अयनं — their original resting place; आपः नारा, नर-सूनवः — waters are nāras, offspring of Nara; अयनं तस्य ताः — they were His first abode.
14.translation: Brahmā identifies Kṛṣṇa Himself as Nārāyaṇa. He is the Self and support of all embodied beings: the aggregate of living beings are ‘nāra,’ and He in whom they rest is Nārāyaṇa. He is also their supreme mover, the one from whom their activity proceeds, and the witness who directly knows every world. Even Nārāyaṇa in the commonly cited cosmogonic sense—the Person whose first abode is the waters or the principles born from Nara—is a manifestation of Kṛṣṇa. The traditional derivations of the name therefore do not limit Him.

15.word_for_word: अपरिच्छेदम् एव उपपादयति — he establishes that the Lord is not spatially delimited; जगद्-आश्रय-भूतं तव वपुः जल-स्थम् यदि सत्यं स्यात् — if Your world-supporting body were literally confined to the cosmic waters; कमल-नाल-मार्गेण अन्तः प्रविश्य संवत्सर-शतं विचिन्वता मया — when I entered through the lotus stalk and searched for a hundred years; किम् इति न दृष्टम् — why did I not find it?; हृदि अपि किम् इति न व्यदर्शि — why was it not seen in the heart either?; तपः-करणानन्तरं सपदि सुदृष्टम् — after austerity it was immediately seen clearly; अतः माया एव — therefore the spatial manifestation is māyā; त्वन्-मूर्तेः देश-विशेष-परिच्छेदः सत्यः न — Your form is not truly limited to a particular place.
15.translation: Brahmā argues that the Lord’s form cannot be spatially delimited. If the body that supports the universe were literally confined to the cosmic waters, why did Brahmā fail to find it when he entered through the lotus-stalk and searched for a hundred years? Nor did he immediately see it within his own heart. Yet after austerity it appeared at once. The apparent localization is therefore a manifestation of māyā; the Lord’s form is not truly bounded by any particular place.

16.word_for_word: यदि जलादि-प्रपञ्चः सत्यः स्यात् — if the world of water and the other elements were independently real; तेन तव परिच्छेदः भवेत् — it would impose limitation upon You; स तु माया-विलसितः — but it is a play of māyā; त्वयैव दर्शितम् — You Yourself demonstrated this; हे माया-धमन — O suppressor of māyā; बहिः स्फुटस्य अपि स्व-जठर-मध्ये जनन्याः प्रदर्शनेन — by showing Your mother within Your belly the very world that was plainly visible outside.
16.translation: If the elemental world possessed independent reality, it would limit the Lord. But Kṛṣṇa Himself demonstrated that it is a display of māyā. O suppressor of māyā, though the world was visibly spread outside Him, He showed that same world to His mother within His own belly.

17.word_for_word: बहिः सतः एव अन्तर्-जठरे प्रतिबिम्बः अस्तु — objection: perhaps the external world was merely reflected inside His belly; यस्य तव कुक्षौ सर्वम् इदं यथा भाति, बहिः अपि तथैव — everything appears within You exactly as it appears outside; सात्मं त्वत्-सहितं सर्वं त्वयि — even the whole that includes You appears within You; मायया विना किं घटते — how could that occur without māyā?; प्रतिबिम्बः चेत् बाह्यात् विलोमतया प्रतीयेत — a reflection should appear reversed relative to the external object; तव च आदर्श-स्थानीयस्य त्वयि प्रतीतिः न स्यात् — and You, the supposed mirror, should not Yourself appear within the reflection; अतः सर्वथा मिथ्यात्वम् — thus it cannot be a simple literal reflection.
17.translation: One might say that the outer world was merely reflected inside Kṛṣṇa’s belly. Śrīdhara rejects this. Everything appeared within Him exactly as outside, and the totality appearing within Him included Kṛṣṇa Himself. A mere reflection should be reversed, and the mirror itself should not appear as part of its own reflection. Thus the vision cannot be explained as an ordinary physical reflection; it is a manifestation of the Lord’s māyā.

18.word_for_word: न केवलं जनन्या, मम अपि तथैव दर्शितम् — not only to Your mother; the same has just been shown to me; त्वद्-ऋते अस्य विश्वस्य मायात्वं — that the universe apart from You is māyā; अद्य एव दर्शितम् — was shown to me today; एकः असि — You were one; ततः मया सह अखिलैः तत्त्वादिभिः उपासिताः तावन्तः चतुर्-भुजाः असि — then You became innumerable four-armed forms worshiped by me and all the principles/deities; जगन्ति ब्रह्माण्डानि अपि दृष्टानि — countless universes too were seen.
18.translation: The same truth was shown not only to Yaśodā but to Brahmā himself that very day: apart from Kṛṣṇa, the universe has the character of māyā. Kṛṣṇa stood as one cowherd boy and then appeared as innumerable four-armed forms worshiped by Brahmā and by all the cosmic principles and deities; Brahmā also beheld innumerable universes. Thus the teaching was directly displayed before him.

19.word_for_word: अद्वितीये त्वयि नानात्वम् — plurality appearing in You who are nondual; गुणावतार-मत्स्यादि-अवतारेषु इव कार्य-वशेन — as in the guṇa-avatāras and Matsya and other descents, according to the work to be done; स्वतन्त्र-माया-निबन्धनम् — depends upon Your independent māyā; त्वत्-पदवीं अजानताम् — for those who do not know Your true nature; अनात्मनि प्रकृतौ स्थितः आत्मा एव त्वम् — You, the Self, appear as though situated in non-Self prakṛti; आत्मना एव स्वातन्त्र्येण मायां वितत्य भासि — by Your own freedom You spread māyā and manifest; सृष्टौ अहम् इव, पालने एष त्वम् इव, अन्ते त्रि-नेत्र इव — in creation like Brahmā, in preservation like Viṣṇu, and at the end like three-eyed Rudra.
19.translation: The consciousness Kṛṣṇa revealed is pure, yet plurality can appear in the nondual Lord through His own independent māyā, just as He assumes the guṇa-avatāras and Matsya and other forms according to the task to be performed. To those who do not know His true nature, the one Self appears as if situated in material prakṛti and, by His own freedom, manifests as the creator like Brahmā, the preserver like Viṣṇu, and the destroyer like three-eyed Rudra.

20.word_for_word: सुरेषु उपेन्द्रः — among the gods, Upendra/Vāmana; ऋषिषु परशुरामः — among the seers, Paraśurāma; नृषु अपि रामः — among human beings, Rāma.
20.translation: Among the gods He appears as Upendra, among the seers as Paraśurāma, and among human beings as Rāma.

21.word_for_word: स्वातन्त्र्ये कथं मत्स्यादिषु जन्म — if You are independent, why take births such as a fish?; कथं वामनादौ याच्ञादि कार्पण्यम् — why in Vāmana and other forms display begging and apparent lowliness?; कथं भय-पलायनादि — why sometimes show fear and flight?; को वेत्ति — who can know?; भूमन् इत्यादिभिः दुर्ज्ञेयत्वम् — the vocatives such as ‘O Infinite One’ stress Your unknowability; भवतः ऊतीः लीलाः त्रि-लोक्यां को वेत्ति — who in the three worlds knows Your līlās?; क्व, कथं, कदा, कति — where, how, when, or how many?; अचिन्त्यं योग-माया-वैभवम् — the power of Your yogamāyā is inconceivable.
21.translation: If the Lord is absolutely free, why does He take forms that seem lowly, such as a fish? Why does Vāmana beg? Why does Kṛṣṇa at times appear afraid or flee? Brahmā’s answer is simply: who can know? The vocatives such as ‘O Infinite One’ emphasize that His līlās cannot be circumscribed. Who in the three worlds can say where they appear, how they operate, when they occur, or how many there are? The majesty of His yogamāyā is inconceivable.

22.word_for_word: प्रपञ्चस्य असत्त्वे कथं सत्त्व-प्रतीतिः — if the phenomenal world lacks independent reality, why does it appear real?; अस्त-धिषणम् — whose apparent cognition has been negated; त्वयि एव उद्यत् उद्भवत् अपि नश्यत् — arising in You and disappearing again; सत् इव — appearing as though real; नित्यम् इव, सुखम् इव, चेतनम् इव — appearing as though permanent, blissful and conscious; अधिष्ठान-भूतस्य तव गुणैः — because of the qualities of You, its underlying support; तथा तथा भाति — it appears in those ways.
22.translation: Brahmā now addresses how an independently unreal world can nevertheless appear real. The entire display arises in Kṛṣṇa and disappears in Him, yet seems real, lasting, pleasurable and conscious because its underlying support is the truly existent, eternal, blissful and conscious Lord. The phenomenal appearance borrows these seeming qualities from its ground.

23.word_for_word: एकः त्वं सत्यः — You alone are real; आत्मा — because You are the Self, never an object seen; दृश्यम् असत्यं — what is merely seen is not ultimately real; आद्यं कारणम् — You are the original cause, therefore unborn; पुराणः पुरा अपि नवः — ancient yet ever new, existing before all effects; पुरुषः — the primordial Person; नित्यः — eternal, excluding post-birth change; पूर्णः — full, excluding increase; अजस्र-सुखः — unceasing bliss, excluding transformation; अक्षरः — undecaying, excluding diminution; अमृतः — deathless, excluding destruction; अनन्तः — unlimited by space and time; अद्वयः — not limited by another entity; स्वयं-ज्योतिः — self-luminous, not attained as a new object through knowledge; निरञ्जनः — stainless, requiring no purification; उपाधितः मुक्तः — free from limiting adjuncts, requiring no transformation through their removal.
23.translation: Kṛṣṇa alone is ultimately real because He is the Self rather than an object merely seen. He is the original cause and therefore is not born; He is ancient yet ever new, existing before every effect. ‘Eternal’ excludes the change of coming into post-birth existence; ‘full’ excludes increase; ‘unceasing bliss’ excludes transformation; ‘imperishable’ excludes diminution; and ‘deathless’ excludes destruction. He is infinite, beyond limitation by space and time, and nondual, beyond limitation by another thing. He is self-luminous, so knowledge does not newly produce or acquire Him; stainless, so no purification can improve Him; and free from limiting adjuncts, so no removal of adjuncts produces a new state in Him.

24.word_for_word: एवं-भूत-ज्ञानात् मुच्यन्ते — by such knowledge beings are liberated; त्वां ये विचक्षते — those who see You correctly; आत्मात्मतया — as the inner Self of the individual self; स-कलात्मनाम् अपि स्वात्मानम् — as the own Self of all selves; गुरुः एव अर्कः — the guru is the sun; तस्मात् लब्धम् उपनिषद्-ज्ञानं सु-चक्षुः — the Upaniṣadic knowledge received from him is the clear eye; भवः अनृताम्बुधिः — saṃsāra is an ocean of unreality; तं तरन्ति इव — they cross it, as it were.
24.translation: Those who see Kṛṣṇa correctly as the innermost Self of their own self and as the own Self of all selves are liberated. The guru is the sun, and the Upaniṣadic knowledge received from him is the clear eye by which this is seen. With that vision they cross the unreal ocean of saṃsāra—or, more precisely, they appear to cross it, since later verses explain that bondage itself was never ultimately real.

25.word_for_word: आत्मानम् एव आत्मतया — knowing the Self precisely as Self; ज्ञानेन तरन्ति — they cross by knowledge; अज्ञान-मूलत्वात् बन्धस्य — because bondage is rooted in ignorance; तेन एव अज्ञानेन प्रपञ्चितः प्रपञ्चः — the world-display is projected by that very ignorance; रज्ज्वाम् अहेः भोग-भवाभवौ — like the superimposition and sublation of a snake upon a rope.
25.translation: The claim that one crosses by knowledge is established because bondage is rooted in ignorance. The phenomenal world, in this analysis, is elaborated by that ignorance itself. Its appearance and disappearance are like the superimposition of a snake upon a rope and its subsequent negation. Therefore knowledge of the Self precisely as Self is the means of ‘crossing.’

26.word_for_word: अज्ञानेन संज्ञा ययोः — bondage and liberation receive their very names through ignorance; भव-बन्ध-मोक्षौ — bondage in becoming and release from it; ऋत-ज्ञ-भावात् अन्यौ न स्तः — they are not realities apart from the state of true knowing; अखण्डानुभव-रूपे परे शुद्धे आत्मनि — in the pure supreme Self, whose nature is unbroken experience; अज्ञानं न, बन्धः न — there is no ignorance and no bondage; अत एव ज्ञानं न, मोक्षः न — therefore no newly arising knowledge and no newly produced liberation; तरणौ सूर्ये रात्र्य्-अहनी इव — like night and day in relation to the sun.
26.translation: Why say that the knower only ‘seems’ to cross? Because the very concepts of bondage and liberation belong to the standpoint of ignorance; they are not independent realities apart from true awareness. In the pure supreme Self, whose nature is unbroken experience, there is no ignorance and therefore no bondage; correspondingly there is no newly produced knowledge or liberation. They are like night and day in relation to the sun.

27.word_for_word: परमार्थ-ज्ञानाद् बन्धो निवर्तताम् — one might say bondage ends through true knowledge in general; आत्मात्मतया ज्ञानाद् इति को आग्रहः — why insist specifically on knowing the Self as Self?; यद्-अध्यासात् आत्मनः पर-रूप-स्फूर्तिः — because through superimposition the Self appears as something other, the body and so forth; तद्-अपवादेन तत्र एव ज्ञानं युक्तम् — knowledge must arise by negating that superimposition in the very locus where it occurred; त्वाम् आत्मानं परं देहादि-रूपं मत्वा — taking You, the Self, to be the alien form of body and so on; आत्मनि देहादिम् अध्यस्य — superimposing body upon Self; देहादौ आत्मानम् अध्यस्य — and Self upon body; ‘नष्ट आत्मा बहिः मृग्यते’ — then seeking the ‘lost’ Self outside; गृहे नष्टं वने न मृग्यते — what is lost in a house is not sought in a forest.
27.translation: Why insist that liberation comes from knowing the Self specifically as Self? Because the error itself consists in superimposition: the Self is taken to be body and other non-Self, while Selfhood is projected onto body and other objects. The error must therefore be negated where it has been imposed. Otherwise one absurdly treats the Self as lost and searches outside for it—like looking in a forest for something lost inside one’s own house.

28.word_for_word: विवेकिनः प्रत्यक् स्वरूपे एव परमात्मानं विचिन्वन्ति — discriminating people search for the Supreme Self within the inward Self; चिज्-जडात्मकं शरीरं तन्-मध्य एव — within the body compounded of sentient and insentient factors; अतत् जडं त्यजन्तः अपवदन्तः — discarding/negating what is insentient and not the Self; अध्यस्त-अपवादं विना अधिष्ठान-तत्त्वं न ज्ञायते — the underlying reality is not known without negating what has been superimposed; समीपे असन्तम् अहिम् निषिध्य — unless one negates the nonexistent snake imagined nearby; सन्तं गुणं रज्जुं न जानन्ति — one does not recognize the existing rope.
28.translation: The discriminating therefore seek the Supreme Self inwardly, within the embodied field, while negating the insentient factors that are not Self. The underlying reality cannot be recognized without removing the superimposition placed upon it. Just as one does not clearly recognize the actually existing rope until the imagined snake has been denied, liberation requires knowledge of the Self as precisely the Self.

29.word_for_word: ज्ञानैक-साध्ये मोक्षे किम् इति भक्तिः — if liberation is achieved by knowledge, why has devotion been emphasized?; तव पादाम्बुज-द्वय-मध्ये एक-देशस्य अपि प्रसाद-लेशः — even the slightest particle of grace from a single part of Your two lotus feet; तेन अनुगृहीतः एव — only one favored by that grace; तव महिम्नः तत्त्वं जानाति — knows the truth of Your greatness; एकः अपि कश्चित् अपि चिरम् विचिन्वन् अपि — anyone else, even searching for a very long time; अतद्-अंश-अपवादेन विचारयन् अपि — even reasoning by negating everything that is not You; न जानाति — cannot know it.
29.translation: If knowledge is the means of liberation, why insist on devotion? Because the truth of Bhagavān’s own greatness is known only by one who receives even the slightest trace of grace from His lotus feet. Another person may inquire for an immense time and reason by negating everything that is not the Lord, yet without that grace he does not know the Lord’s majesty in truth.

30.word_for_word: तस्मात् भूरि-भागः — therefore the great good fortune I ask for; अत्र भवे ब्रह्म-जन्मनि — in this existence, whether a birth as Brahmā; तिरश्चाम् अपि मध्ये यत् जन्म — or even a birth among animals; येन भाग्येन भवदीयानां जनानाम् एकः भूत्वा — by which I might become even one among Your people; निषेवे अत्यर्थं सेवेये — and serve You intensely.
30.translation: Therefore Brahmā asks only for this great fortune: whether born again as Brahmā or even among animals, may he somehow become one among the Lord’s own people and serve Him completely.

31.word_for_word: त्वद्-भक्तिमत्-जन्म एव श्रेष्ठम् — any birth endowed with devotion to You is superior even to divine birth; व्रज-गो-रमण्यः — the cows of Vraja and the beautiful cowherd women; त्वया वत्सतर-आत्मज-आत्मना — by You in the forms of their calves and sons; यस्य तव तृप्तये सर्वे यज्ञाः अद्यापि न शक्ताः — all sacrifices are still unable fully to satisfy You; तेन त्वया प्रतिक्षणं तृप्यता — yet You were satisfied by them moment after moment; यासां स्तन्यम् अमृत-रूपं पीतम् — drinking their nectar-like milk.
31.translation: Any birth that carries devotion to Kṛṣṇa is higher even than a divine birth. How blessed were the cows and women of Vraja: Kṛṣṇa became their calves and sons and drank their nectar-like milk at every moment. All the sacrifices of the world cannot fully satisfy Him, yet He accepted satisfaction again and again from their breasts.

32.word_for_word: अहो इति पुनर् उक्त्या — by repeating the exclamation ‘aho’; भाग्यस्य सर्वथा अपरिच्छिन्नत्वम् — Brahmā indicates that their fortune is altogether immeasurable.
32.translation: The renewed exclamation ‘aho!’ expresses that the good fortune of the people of Vraja cannot be delimited at all.

33.word_for_word: शर्वादयः ... वयं च — Śiva and the other presiding deities, and Brahmā himself; मनो-बुद्ध्य्-अहङ्कार-चक्षुर्-आद्य्-अधिष्ठातारः त्रयोदश-देवाः — the thirteen deities presiding over mind, intellect, ego and the senses; हृषीकाणि इन्द्रियाणि एव चषकाणि — the senses themselves are our drinking cups; चित्ताधिष्ठातुः अङ्घ्री उदजे — the lotus feet of the Lord who presides over consciousness; तयोर् मधु मकरन्दः अमृतं स्वादु आसवम् — their honey is nectar, a sweet intoxicating drink; पिबामः — we drink it; प्रत्येकम् इन्द्रियाभिमानिनः एक-देश-सेविनः अपि कृतार्थाः — even we, presiding over only one sense or function, are fulfilled by serving one portion of Him; सर्वेन्द्रियैः सर्व-सेविनाम् एतेषां किं वर्ण्यते भाग्यम् — what, then, can be said of those residents of Vraja who serve Him with all their senses?.
33.translation: Brahmā says that he, Śiva and the other presiding deities of mind, intellect, ego and the senses are already immeasurably fortunate. Their respective senses are like cups by which they drink the sweet intoxicating nectar—the honey of the Lord’s lotus feet. If each cosmic deity is fulfilled merely by serving one aspect of Him through one governing faculty, what words can describe the fortune of the Vraja residents who serve Him completely with all their senses?

34.word_for_word: तद् भूरि-भाग्यम् — that is the great fortune I asked for; मनुष्य-लोके यत् किम् अपि जन्म — any birth in the human realm; अटव्यां — especially in the forest region; गोकुले — especially in Gokula; कतमस्य अपि अङ्घ्रि-रजः-अभिषेकम् — so that I might be bathed in the foot-dust of any one resident of Gokula; येषां जीवितं निखिलं भगवान् मुकुन्दः — whose entire life is Bhagavān Mukunda; श्रुति-मृग्यम् — sought even by the Vedas; मृग्यते एव न तु दृश्यते — searched for but not fully seen.
34.translation: This is the ‘great fortune’ Brahmā asks for: any birth at all in this human world, more specifically in the forest land of Gokula, if only he can be bathed in the foot-dust of any resident there. Their entire life is Bhagavān Mukunda alone. He whom even the Vedas continue to seek without fully seeing is the very center of their daily existence.

35.word_for_word: येषां भक्त्या भवान् अपि ऋणी इव आस्ते — by whose devotion even You seem indebted; किं विश्व-फलात् सर्व-फलात्मकात् त्वत्तः परं फलं राता दास्यति — what reward beyond You, the totality of all rewards, could anyone give them?; नः चेतः मुह्यति — my mind is bewildered by this question; सद्-वेष-अनुकरण-मात्रेण पापिष्ठा पूतना अपि त्वाम् एव आपिता — even sinful Pūtanā attained You merely by imitating the guise of a good nurse; स-कुला बकाघासुर-सहिता — and her whole family, including Baka and Agha, received extraordinary benefit; येषां धामादयः त्वत्-कृते — while the homes and everything of the Vraja residents exist solely for Your sake.
35.translation: How can the fulfillment of these devotees be described when even Bhagavān seems indebted to their devotion? What reward beyond Kṛṣṇa Himself—the sum of every possible fruit—could be given to them? Brahmā’s mind is bewildered. Even the wicked Pūtanā attained the Lord merely by imitating the appearance of a loving nurse, and her family, including Baka and Agha, received astonishing benefit. How then could even Kṛṣṇa’s giving Himself be an adequate return to Nanda and the people of Vraja, whose homes, possessions and entire lives exist only for Him?

36.word_for_word: रागादयः तावद् एव स्तेनाः — attachment and the other passions are thieves only so long; गृहम् तावद् एव कारा-गृहं — home is a prison only so long; मोहः तावद् एव अङ्घ्रि-निगडः — delusion is a fetter on the feet only so long; यावत् ते त्वदीया जना न भवन्ति — as long as people have not become Yours; त्वदीयानां तु रागादयः अपि त्वन्-निष्ठाः मोचकाः एव — for Your people even attachment and the other emotions, being fixed on You, become liberating; यतिभ्यः न विशेषः, भजनं तु अधिकम् — they lose nothing compared with renunciants, while their devotion is greater.
36.translation: Attachment and the other passions are thieves only until a person belongs to Kṛṣṇa; a house is a prison only until then, and delusion a chain around the feet only until then. For those who are His, even attachments become centered on Him and therefore serve liberation. The residents of Vraja are not spiritually inferior to renunciants merely because they possess homes and relationships; rather, their devotion is greater.

37.word_for_word: अहम् एषां पुत्रादि-रूपेण वर्ते — objection: I already exist as their sons and relations; प्रपन्ना जनता — the surrendered community; आनन्दानां सन्दोहं प्रथयितुम् — to expand the mass of their bliss; कपट-पुत्रत्वादिना — merely by assuming the role of their son; तादृग् भक्तेः आनृण्यम् न संपद्यते — such a role does not discharge the debt owed to devotion of that magnitude.
37.translation: If Kṛṣṇa says, ‘I already live among them as their son and relative,’ Brahmā replies that these roles serve to expand the flood of happiness experienced by His surrendered people. Merely playing at being their son does not discharge the debt created by devotion of such magnitude.

38.word_for_word: आदितः आरभ्य अचिन्त्य-अनन्त-गुणत्वेन स्वयं दुर्ज्ञेयत्वम् उक्तम् — from the beginning His unknowability due to inconceivably infinite qualities has been stated; ‘जानीम’ इति स्थितान् उपहसन् — almost laughing at those who claim ‘we know Him’; न तु मे मन-आदीनां तव वैभवं विषयः — Your majesty is not an object accessible to my mind and faculties.
38.translation: From the beginning Brahmā has said that Kṛṣṇa cannot be comprehended because His qualities are inconceivable and infinite. He now almost mocks those who confidently say, ‘We know Him.’ Kṛṣṇa’s majesty is not an object that Brahmā’s mind or other faculties can circumscribe.

39.word_for_word: जगद्-ईशत्वाद्य्-अभिमानं परित्यज्य — abandoning pride in being lord of the universe; अनुजानीहि — grant me leave; स्व-महिमानम् अस्मद्-आदीनां ज्ञान-बलादि सर्वं त्वम् एव वेत्सि — You alone know Your glory and all the knowledge and power of beings such as us; सर्व-दृक् जगतां नाथः त्वम् एव — You alone are the all-seeing Lord of the worlds; ममतास्पदं जगद् एतत् शरीरं च तव अर्पितम् — this universe and this body, which I had treated as ‘mine,’ are offered back to You.
39.translation: Brahmā abandons his pride of cosmic lordship and asks permission to depart. Kṛṣṇa alone knows His own majesty and the full extent of the knowledge and strength of Brahmā and every other being. He alone is the all-seeing Lord of all worlds. Therefore Brahmā offers back to Him both the universe and the body that he had mistakenly regarded as his own.

40.word_for_word: किङ्करं मां प्रस्थापय — send me away as Your servant; श्री-कृष्ण — O Śrī Kṛṣṇa; वृष्णि-कुल-पद्मस्य प्रीति-दातृत्वेन सूर्योपम — like the sun giving delight to the lotus of the Vṛṣṇi clan; क्ष्मा-निर्जर-द्विज-पशु-उदधीनां वृद्धि-कारित्वेन चन्द्रोपम — like the moon causing increase for earth, gods, brāhmaṇas and cattle; उद्धर्म-शार्वर-तमो-हर — remover of the night-darkness of false religion; क्षिति-राक्षस-ध्रुक् — enemy of the Rākṣasas on earth, like the rising sun; आर्कम् अर्कम् अभिव्याप्य — surpassing and pervading even the sun; सर्वेषाम् अर्हन् — worthy of worship by all; आकल्पं ते नमः — homage to You until the end of the kalpa; स-सखि-वत्सक-मोक्षण-कौतुक... — may Acyuta, who for the joy of His friends and calves assumed all their forms, protect you and increase Vraja’s auspiciousness.
40.translation: With great reverence Brahmā bows and asks, ‘Send me forth now as Your servant.’ Kṛṣṇa is like the sun bringing delight to the lotus of the Vṛṣṇi clan, and like the moon bringing increase to the earth, gods, brāhmaṇas and cattle. He dispels the nocturnal darkness of false religion and rises against the Rākṣasas of the earth like the sun—yet even the sun is an inadequate comparison, for He pervades and surpasses it and is worshipful to all. ‘May my homage be Yours until the end of the kalpa.’ Śrīdhara’s concluding verse prays that Acyuta, who for the joy connected with the liberation of His friends and calves assumed all their forms, protect the hearers and bring auspiciousness to Vraja.

41.word_for_word: पादयोः नत्वा — bowing at His two feet; अभीष्टम् — desired; सर्वतः पूजितम् अभिप्रेतं वा — universally honored, or intended/desirable.
41.translation: Brahmā bowed at Kṛṣṇa’s two feet. The expression may mean ‘the desired object,’ or that which is honored on every side and held most dear.

42.word_for_word: अनुज्ञाप्य — obtaining permission; अनुज्ञां प्रदाप्य पृष्ट्वा — having asked and received leave; स्व-भुवं ब्रह्माणम् — the self-born Brahmā; यथा-पूर्वं सखायः यस्मिन् तत् स्वकं पुलिनम् — the same riverbank where His friends remained as before; प्राग्-अवस्थितान् वत्सान् आनिन्ये — He brought back the calves, restored to their former position.
42.translation: After Brahmā asked for and received permission to depart, Kṛṣṇa returned to His own riverbank, where His friends were just as they had been before, and brought the original calves back to them.

43.word_for_word: एतावन्तं कालं कथं तत्रैव उपविष्टाः — how could they remain seated there through so much time?; कथं क्षुत्-पिपासादि-विस्मरणम् — how did they forget hunger and thirst?; अब्दे अपि याते — although a year had passed; प्राणेशं कृष्णम् अन्तरा — separated from Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of their life; प्रिय-विरहे क्षणः अपि वर्षाधिकः — in separation from a beloved even a moment seems longer than a year; तथापि माया-हताः क्षणार्धं मेनिरे — nevertheless, struck by His māyā, they regarded the whole year as half a moment.
43.translation: How had the boys remained seated there and forgotten hunger and thirst for so long? Although a year had passed, they had been separated from Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of their life—and normally even one moment of separation from a beloved seems longer than a year. Yet Kṛṣṇa’s māyā had covered the interval, so they experienced the entire year as no more than half a moment.

44.word_for_word: यया मायया मोहितं जगत् — by that māyā the world is deluded; अभीक्ष्णं पुनः पुनः — repeatedly, again and again; विस्मृतात्मकम् — made forgetful of its own Self; विस्मृत आत्मा एव येन तत् — that by which the Self itself is forgotten.
44.translation: It is that same māyā by which the world is repeatedly deluded and made to forget its own Self.

45.word_for_word: त्वया अतिवेगेन स्वागतम् — you have returned very quickly; सम्यक् आगतम् — welcome back; एकः अपि ग्रासः त्वां विना अस्माभिः न अभोजि — we have not eaten even one morsel without you; इत एहि — come here; साधु अविक्षेपेण भुज्यताम् — now eat properly without distraction.
45.translation: The boys greeted Kṛṣṇa as though He had only just left: ‘You came back very quickly—welcome! We have not eaten even a single morsel without You. Come here and now eat properly with us, without any further interruption.’

46.word_for_word: अभ्यवहृत्य — having eaten; भुक्त्वा — having taken His meal.
46.translation: ‘Abhyavahṛtya’ means ‘having eaten’ or ‘having taken the meal.’

47.word_for_word: प्रोद्दामो वेणु-आदिः — the loudly sounding flute and other instruments; तस्य रवैः उत्सवः तेन आढ्यः — splendid with the festivity produced by their sounds; गृणन् — calling aloud; उपलालनैः आह्वयन् — calling the calves affectionately; गोपी-दृशाम् उत्सव-रूपा दृशिः यस्य — whose very sight was a festival for the eyes of the gopīs.
47.translation: The return became a festival rich with the loud sounds of flute and other instruments. Kṛṣṇa called the calves with affectionate cries, and His very appearance was a festival for the eyes of the gopīs.

48.word_for_word: यशोदा-नन्द-सूनुना — by the son of Yaśodā and Nanda; बहूनाम् उक्तिः सहैव दर्शिता — the wording can indicate both parents together; केचित् यशोदा-सूनुना, अपरे नन्द-सूनुना — some explain ‘son of Yaśodā,’ others ‘son of Nanda’; यद् वा यशोदां नन्दयति इति यशोदा-नन्दः — alternatively, ‘he who delights Yaśodā’; अस्मान् महा-व्यालात् अविता — He protected us from the great serpent.
48.translation: The expression ‘Yaśodā-Nanda-sūnu’ can refer jointly to the son of Yaśodā and Nanda; some construe it as ‘Yaśodā’s son’ and others as ‘Nanda’s son.’ Alternatively it can mean ‘the son who gives joy to Yaśodā.’ The boys proclaimed that this very child had protected them from the great serpent.

49.word_for_word: स्व-तोकेषु स्नेह-वल्ली अब्दम् अन्वहम् निःसीम ववृधे — for a year the vine of affection toward their own children increased without limit; यथा कृष्णे तु अपूर्ववत् — just as their unprecedented love had been directed toward Kṛṣṇa; स्व-तोकेभ्यः अपि पर-पुत्रे कृष्णे प्रेमाधिक्यम् — previously they loved Kṛṣṇa, another’s son, even more than their own children; तत्र पृच्छति — the king now asks about this.
49.translation: The earlier account said that for an entire year the residents’ affection for their own children grew without limit, becoming like their unprecedented love for Kṛṣṇa; indeed they had formerly loved Kṛṣṇa, technically another’s son, even more than their own. The king now asks for the reason.

50.word_for_word: श्री-कृष्णस्य साक्षात् आत्मत्वात् — because Śrī Kṛṣṇa is directly the Self; तस्मिन् आत्मीयेभ्यः प्रेमाधिक्यं युज्यते — it is natural that He be loved more than things merely connected with the self; आत्मनः स्वतः प्रेष्ठत्वम् — the Self is dear in itself; अन्येषां तु तद्-उपाधिकम् — other things are dear only because of their relation to it; पञ्चभिः दर्शयति — he demonstrates this in five verses.
50.translation: Śrīdhara answers that Śrī Kṛṣṇa is directly the Self, so it is entirely fitting that love for Him exceed love for things merely related to oneself. The Self is dear by its own nature; everything else is dear only because of its connection with the Self. The next five verses establish this.

51.word_for_word: तथा-दर्शनात् — because experience shows this; स्व-स्वक-आत्मनि — in one’s own self; अहङ्कार-आस्पदे देहे — in the body, which is the locus of the ‘I’-notion.
51.translation: The point is established by ordinary experience: even the body, the immediate locus of the ‘I’-sense, is loved because it is taken as one’s self.

52.word_for_word: आत्माध्यास-तारतम्येन प्रेम-तारतम्यम् — gradations of love correspond to gradations of superimposed selfhood; मूढ-अमूढ-भेदेन — he distinguishes the confused from the discriminating; देहात्म-वादिनाम् — for those who identify the body as the self; तं देहम् अनु भवन्ति ये पुत्रादयः — sons and others who arise in relation to that body; न तथा प्रियतमा — are not as dear as the body/self itself.
52.translation: Differences in affection follow the degree to which selfhood is superimposed. Even for those who identify the body with the self, sons and other relations that arise in connection with that body are not as dear as the body taken to be ‘I.’ Śrīdhara then distinguishes the confused from the discriminating.

53.word_for_word: जीर्यति अपि आसन्न-मरणे अपि जीविताशा भवति — even when the body is decaying and death is near, the wish to live persists; न जीविष्यति इति निश्चिते अपि देहे यत् प्रेमास्पदत्वम् — even when one knows the body will not survive it remains an object of love; तत् आत्म-गतम् एव — that love actually belongs to the self projected onto it; न तु देह-गतम् — not to the body as such, which is dying and even becoming repulsive; विवेकिनः यदा ममता-भाग् भवति — for the discriminating, when the body is recognized merely as something ‘mine’; आत्मवत् प्रियो न भवति — it is no longer dear like the Self.
53.translation: Even when the body is worn out and death is near, the wish to live remains. The affection felt even for a body known to be dying does not belong to the body as such—indeed the body may already be repulsive—but to the self that has been projected upon it. When a discriminating person recognizes the body merely as ‘mine’ rather than ‘I,’ it no longer possesses the same dearness as the Self.

54.word_for_word: तद्-अर्थम् एव सकलं प्रियम् — everything is dear only for the sake of that Self.
54.translation: Thus every other thing is dear only for the sake of the Self.

55.word_for_word: प्रस्तुतम् आह — he applies the principle to the subject at hand; कृष्णम् एनम् इति — with the words ‘this Kṛṣṇa.’
55.translation: He now applies that principle directly to the subject under discussion with the words ‘this Kṛṣṇa.’

56.word_for_word: न केवलम् आत्मनाम् आत्मा — He is not only the Self of living selves; जडानाम् अपि — He is also the ground of insentient things; सर्व-जगत्-कारणम् इति कृष्णं जानतां पुंसाम् — for those who know Kṛṣṇa as the cause of the whole universe; स्थावरं जङ्गमं च सर्वम् — everything stationary and moving; भगवद्-रूपम् — is a form of Bhagavān; भगवान् एव स्वरूपं यस्य — its true nature is none other than Bhagavān; न अन्यत् — not something separate.
56.translation: Kṛṣṇa is not merely the Self of conscious beings; He is also the ground of insentient reality. For those who know Him as the cause of the entire universe, everything moving and unmoving is understood as a form whose true basis is Bhagavān Himself, not as something wholly separate from Him.

57.word_for_word: भावार्थः सद्-रूपार्थः परमार्थः — the ‘true meaning’ is the reality that has being, the ultimate truth; परिणामिनि कारणे स्थितः — an effect is grounded in its transforming material cause; ‘वाचारम्भणं विकारो नाम-धेयं मृत्तिका इत्य् एव सत्यम्’ — ‘a modification is only a verbal designation; clay alone is real’; तस्य कारणस्य अपि भगवान् कृष्णः भवत्-कारणम् — Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa is in turn the cause even of that causal substrate; अतः किम् अतत् — what, then, is not He?; श्री-कृष्ण-व्यतिरिक्तं वस्तु रूप्यताम् — let anyone point out a reality separate from Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
57.translation: The ultimate ‘meaning’ or reality of an effect is the existent cause in which it rests, as the Upaniṣad says: ‘A modification is only a name arising from speech; clay alone is real.’ Yet Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa is the cause even of every such causal substrate. What, then, can truly be said to be ‘not Kṛṣṇa’? Let anyone point out a reality ultimately independent of Him.

58.word_for_word: श्री-कृष्णस्य एव परमार्थत्वात् — because Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone is the ultimate reality; तद्-एक-शरणानाम् अयत्न-सिद्धः मोक्षः — liberation comes effortlessly to those who take refuge in Him alone; पुण्य-यशाः मुरारिः — Murāri of holy fame; पद-पल्लवः एव प्लवः — His tender lotus foot is itself the boat; महत्-पदम् — the abode of the great, or itself the great station; भवाम्बुधिः वत्स-पद-मात्रं — the ocean of becoming becomes no more than the water in a calf’s hoofprint; परं पदं श्री-वैकुण्ठाख्यं स्थानम् — the supreme destination called Śrī Vaikuṇṭha; विपदां पदं न भवति — the realm of calamity never again becomes theirs; न पुनर् आवर्तते — they do not return.
58.translation: Because Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the ultimate reality, liberation is effortlessly accomplished for those who take refuge in Him alone. Murāri’s tender lotus feet are themselves their boat and the abode of the great. For them the ocean of saṃsāra becomes as insignificant as the water held in a calf’s hoofprint; their destination is the supreme abode called Śrī Vaikuṇṭha, and the realm of calamity never becomes theirs again. They do not return.

60.word_for_word: सुहृद्भिः चरितम् — the play with His friends; ‘मुष्णन्तोऽन्योन्य-शिक्यादीन्’ इत्यादिना उक्तम् — described beginning with their stealing one another’s slings; अघार्दनम् — the slaying of Agha; शाद्वले जेमनं भोजनम् — the meal upon the grassy bank; व्यक्तेतरं — other than the manifest insentient world; शुद्ध-सत्त्वात्मकं वत्स-तत्-पाल-रूपम् — the pure-sattva forms of calves and keepers; यद् वा चिद्-विलासः एव रूपम् — alternatively, forms that are direct displays of consciousness; अजस्य उरुः अभिष्टवः — the great praise offered by unborn Brahmā; एतत् शृण्वन् गृणन् गायन् नरः — a person hearing, reciting or singing this; सर्व-पुरुषार्थान् प्राप्नोति — attains all human goals.
60.translation: The chapter has narrated Kṛṣṇa’s play with His friends, beginning with their stealing one another’s slings, the slaying of Aghāsura, the meal on the grassy riverbank, His manifestation as the calves and cowherd boys in forms of pure sattva—indeed as direct displays of consciousness—and the great hymn offered by unborn Brahmā. A person who hears, recites or sings this account attains all the goals of human life.

61.word_for_word: इति श्री-परमानन्द-नृसिंह-पद-षट्पदः — thus, the bee at the feet of Śrī Paramānanda Nṛsiṃha; व्याकरोत् श्रीधर-स्वामी — Śrīdhara Svāmī explained; यथा-मति — according to his understanding; विधि-स्तुतिम् — the hymn of Vidhi, Brahmā.
61.translation: Thus Śrīdhara Svāmī, a bee at the feet of Śrī Paramānanda Nṛsiṃha, has explained according to his understanding the hymn of Vidhi—Brahmā’s prayer to Kṛṣṇa.
